name: Raw accelerometer and gyroscope
plain: Reads raw motion sensor streams with no prompt.
meaning: Accelerometer and gyro readings can infer taps, typing, gait and a device-specific calibration fingerprint. Both OSes cap or restrict background use.

android.persistence: Until app stops or goes to background (API 28 blocks background sensor events)
android.note: Without the permission Android 12 caps accelerometer, gyro and magnetometer at 200 Hz

ios.prompt_ui: None; NSMotionUsageDescription only for activity and pedometer APIs
ios.note: Typical device cap about 100 Hz; background updates stop when suspended

fields.name: rate
fields.range: up to about 200 Hz Android, about 100 Hz iOS

limits.headline: Can see how your phone moves and tilts, with no prompt
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a game, map or app uses motion
can: Get accelerometer and gyroscope readings (tilt and shake)
Use motion for games, steps and compass features
Sample about 100 times a second on iPhone
Sample above 200 times a second on Android if the app declares it
cannot: Sample above 200 Hz on Android 12 and newer without declaring it
Keep going in the background on iPhone; updates stop when the app is suspended
See your location from motion alone
Use motion in Safari on iPhone without a permission since iOS 12.2
limits.reach_label: Motion data, while the app runs
limits.differs: Android 12 caps rate at 200 Hz unless declared. iPhone caps near 100 Hz and stops in the background.

story.what_it_is: An app reads the raw accelerometer and gyroscope, which measure how your phone tilts and shakes.

marketing.name: Motion sensors
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps read motion sensors to detect tilt, shake and rotation.

marketing.name: Core Motion
marketing.pitch: Apple's framework for accelerometer, gyroscope and device motion in apps.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. When you tilt your phone to steer a car, or shake to undo, apps are reading these sensors. The same stream can quietly reveal how you walk, tap or hold the phone.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for steering in games, AR, step counting and shake gestures. The signal can also be used to guess taps, gait and typing, and each chip has a tiny unique error that can mark one phone.

use_cases.example: A racing game lets you steer by tilting the phone.
An AR app keeps its virtual objects fixed in your room by tracking how the phone moves.
A photo app straightens your image using the tilt of the phone.
A step counter finds your steps from the bounce of your walk.
A bank app checks natural hand movement to tell a person from a bot.
A hidden script reads the sensors to build a device fingerprint or guess your taps.

story.android_note: Android 12 limits the speed of these sensors without a special permission, which blunts some attacks.
story.ios_note: iPhone gives no prompt for raw motion on a normal app, and Safari asks for motion access on websites.

technical_bounds: Browsers gate these behind a prompt on iOS Safari
Background access blocked on Android 9 and later
iOS motion activity needs a prompt
